one_liner: Lazy-evaluated C++20 NumPy/PyTorch-style tensor library for CPU and Metal GPU; beats Eigen3 on some unary math ops, loses on others.
what_it_does: Axiom is a NumPy/PyTorch-style tensor library for C++20: operator overloading, broadcasting, einops-style rearrange/reduce, and a lazy computation graph that fuses chained ops and reuses buffers before materializing. It targets CPU (via Apple Accelerate, OpenBLAS, or a portable Highway SIMD/OpenMP path) and Apple Metal GPU, with zero-copy CPU/GPU transfers on Apple Silicon's unified memory. It is not a drop-in for Eigen or std:: containers — the API is whole-tensor with NumPy/PyTorch semantics, not a scalar math-function replacement.
how_it_is_fast: CPU element-wise ops dispatch through three tiers (seen in src/backends/cpu/cpu_operations.cpp): Apple Accelerate/vDSP (vvsinf/vvcosf/vvexpf/vvlogf) on macOS, then Google Highway's portable SIMD kernels (AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/SVE/RVV, see src/backends/cpu/simd/simd_dispatch.hpp) as the cross-platform fallback, then a scalar loop parallelized with OpenMP for large tensors. Matmul/linear algebra route through a BLAS/LAPACK backend (Accelerate, OpenBLAS, or native). A lazy graph compiler fuses chained elementwise operations and reuses buffers to cut materialization and memory traffic.
when_to_use: On macOS/Apple Silicon, want NumPy/PyTorch ergonomics in C++ with a Metal GPU path and zero-copy CPU/GPU transfers
Whole-tensor elementwise math (exp/log/sin/cos) at large sizes (~4096x4096 float32) where Accelerate vForce or Highway SIMD beats Eigen3's own vectorization
Want einops-style rearrange/reduce and a lazy fused computation graph instead of hand-rolled expression templates
Need built-in FFT, numpy/safetensors/flatbuffers IO, or basic NN layers (Linear, Conv, Attention, RNN) alongside tensor math
Can link a built library (CMake, C++20 toolchain) rather than needing a header-only drop-in
when_not_to_use: Need a scalar, single-value <cmath>-style API — Axiom has no fine-grained per-value math entry point
The op is sqrt or tanh specifically — Axiom's own benchmark table shows both slower than Eigen3 on the tested hardware
Off-macOS (Linux/Windows), where the fast path is Highway SIMD + OpenMP, not Accelerate — the published GB/s numbers are macOS/Accelerate-specific and won't transfer as-is
Need GPU acceleration beyond Apple Metal — no CUDA/ROCm backend
Production use requiring API stability — v0.5.1, 114 stars, open issue on CPU-only macOS builds failing to link (#28) and a tracked gap in public-interface docs (#9)

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (CMake FetchContent source-drop; not header-only)
integration.dependencies: bundled: Highway, mimalloc, pocketfft, flatbuffers, nlohmann_json, FP16, FXdiv; optional: OpenBLAS, Apple Accelerate framework (macOS), OpenMP, Metal/MPSGraph (macOS GPU)
integration.platforms: macOS (Accelerate + Metal GPU), Linux, Windows; portable SIMD via Highway (SSE2 through AVX-512, NEON, SVE, RVV)
integration.thread_safety: not documented beyond internally OpenMP-parallelized kernels; no stated guarantee about concurrent access to a single Tensor from multiple threads
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different API model (whole-tensor NumPy/PyTorch semantics, lazy graph) vs Eigen3's expression templates

gotchas: On macOS the measured unary-op speedups over Eigen3 come from Apple Accelerate vForce (vvsinf/vvcosf/vvexpf/vvlogf), not Axiom's own SIMD kernels — the win is largely Accelerate's, not portable
sqrt and tanh are slower than Eigen3 in Axiom's own benchmark table — op-specific, not a blanket win
Open issue #28: CPU-only builds on macOS can fail to link because some Metal call sites guard on __APPLE__ instead of the AXIOM_METAL_SUPPORT flag
Library type follows BUILD_SHARED_LIBS (defaults to SHARED); set it explicitly before FetchContent/add_subdirectory if you need a single static archive
pick_this_over_siblings_when: trigno_simd_cpp, SLEEF, FABE13-HX, fast_math_cpp, fmath, and VDT are scalar/vector math-function libraries meant to drop into existing loops in place of <cmath>/libm calls; Axiom is a whole-tensor library with a lazy graph and GPU path, so pick it only when you also want NumPy/PyTorch-style tensor ops and fusion — not when you just need a faster std::sin/std::exp replacement, where the siblings are the direct fit and Axiom is not.
verified_claims_summary: docs/BENCHMARKS.md (auto-generated 2026-02-21; Test Environment states only 'Darwin 25.3.0 arm64', no CPU model or compiler) reports 4096x4096 float32 unary-op GB/s vs Eigen3: sin 26.0 vs 11.0 (~2.4x), cos 25.2 vs 11.0 (~2.3x), exp 23.0 vs 16.4 (~1.4x), log 17.0 vs 13.1 (~1.3x); the same table shows sqrt (39.0 vs 66.3) and tanh (14.3 vs 21.5) slower than Eigen3. Code confirms macOS sin/cos/exp/log dispatch to Apple Accelerate vForce ahead of Axiom's own Highway kernels, so the measured win largely reflects Accelerate vs Eigen3's own vectorization rather than a novel Axiom algorithm.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-05-29, v0.5.1, MIT) but young and small (114 stars, 5 open issues); 'copyable' usability means a real CMake build with bundled third-party deps, not a single header to vendor.
